title: Conformational flexibility and transient structure of the proline-rich domain in p53.
authors: Berggren, Agnes; Bakker, Michael; Fisher, Hayden; Skepo, Marie
one_liner_zh: 该文用全原子MD模拟结合生物物理实验表征p53脯氨酸富集域的内在无序构象与瞬时PPII结构，虽属蛋白质-DNA互作体系中的p53蛋白结构域，但未涉及DNA结合或互作建模，方法上MD可迁移至TF-DNA动态研究，故为中档。
abstract: The proline-rich domain (PRD) of the tumor suppressor p53 plays a central role in modulating conformational dynamics and molecular interactions, yet its intrinsic structural behavior remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine extensive all-atom molecular dynamics simulations with biophysical validation to characterize the conformational ensemble of the p53 PRD. The domain behaves as an intrinsically disordered region, sampling a highly heterogeneous ensemble with average end-to-end distance and radius of gyration of 52.5 A and 21.8 A, respectively. Despite this disorder, transient local structure is prominent: unordered conformations dominate, followed by substantial polyproline II (PPII) content, with beta-bends and turns linking conserved PXXP motifs. Circular dichroism and small-angle X-ray scattering experiments corroborate the largely disordered yet partially structured nature of the PRD. Ramachandran and contact analyses reveal that consecutive prolines, particularly Pro71-Pro72, impose steric constraints that stabilize locally extended conformations and restrict backbone collapse. To approximate the PRD within full-length p53, additional simulations were performed with restrained terminal distances, yielding reduced conformational variability and improved agreement with small-angle X-ray scattering data while preserving secondary-structure propensities. PPII helices emerge as particularly robust features, acting as stiff spacers linking the transactivation domain to downstream regions. Finally, simulations of clinically relevant variants reveal mutation-specific local perturbations: P72R disrupts consecutive proline rigidity and increases flexibility, whereas P82L abolishes a PXXP motif and its associated PPII helix. These results identify proline-mediated rigidity and transient PPII structure as key determinants of the dynamic conformational landscape of the p53 PRD.
abstract_zh: 肿瘤抑制因子p53的富含脯氨酸结构域（PRD）在调节构象动力学和分子相互作用中发挥核心作用，但其内在结构行为仍未完全阐明。在此，我们结合广泛的全程原子分子动力学模拟与生物物理验证，表征p53 PRD的构象系综。该结构域表现为内在无序区域，采样高度异质性的系综，其平均端到端距离和回旋半径分别为52.5 Å和21.8 Å。尽管存在这种无序性，瞬态局部结构显著：无序构象占主导，随后是大量的聚脯氨酸II（PPII）含量，β-转角（beta-bends）和转折连接保守的PXXP基序。圆二色性和小角X射线散射实验证实了PRD主要无序但部分结构化的性质。拉马钱德兰分析和接触分析揭示，连续脯氨酸，特别是Pro71-Pro72，施加空间约束，稳定局部延伸构象并限制骨架塌缩。为在全长p53中近似PRD，进行了额外模拟，采用受限末端距离，结果减少了构象变异性，并改善了与小角X射线散射数据的一致性，同时保留了二级结构倾向。PPII螺旋作为特别稳健的特征出现，充当连接反式激活结构域与下游区域的刚性间隔物。最后，临床相关变体的模拟揭示了突变特异性局部扰动：P72R破坏连续脯氨酸刚性并增加灵活性，而P82L消除PXXP基序及其相关PPII螺旋。这些结果确定脯氨酸介导的刚性和瞬态PPII结构为p53 PRD动态构象景观的关键决定因素。
